description: The DAG Workflow Editor is a split-pane editor for authoring DAG-based automation workflows in YAML. The left pane hosts a Monaco code editor with YAML syntax highlighting; the right pane shows a live ReactFlow graph that auto-updates as YAML is edited. A toolbar provides workflow naming, file import/export, and a real-time validation status badge. Validation is debounced 500 ms and invokes the Rust backend via the 'validate_dag_workflow' Tauri command. The graph visualises nodes typed as command, prompt, check, ui-bridge, approval, cancel, workflow-ref, or loop — each coloured and iconified distinctly — with dependency edges auto-laid out using dagre. Three overlay states cover the graph pane: empty content, YAML validation errors, and mid-parse. A global ApprovalDialog overlay (mounted at app level) listens for the 'dag:approval-requested' Tauri event and presents Approve / Reject buttons, invoking 'respond_dag_approval' to unblock a waiting DAG approval node during workflow execution.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The DAG Workflow Editor page is mounted inside the tab system with data-page-id='dag-workflow-editor'. It renders a full-height flex column: toolbar at top, split-pane body in the middle, and a status bar at the bottom.

assertions.description: The page root element with data-page-id='dag-workflow-editor' is present and fills the available viewport height.
The toolbar row containing the workflow name input, Import/Export buttons, and validation badge is visible at the top of the page.
The left pane has a panel header reading 'YAML Editor'.
The right pane has a panel header reading 'DAG Graph'.
The status bar at the bottom of the page always shows the fixed text 'DAG Workflow Editor'.

groups.name: Toolbar Controls
groups.description: The toolbar contains a workflow name input field (aria-label='Workflow name'), an Import button, an Export button, and a validation status badge. These are the primary controls for managing a workflow file.

assertions.description: An editable text input with aria-label='Workflow name' is present in the toolbar. On page load it defaults to 'My Workflow' (from the default YAML template).
An 'Import' button is present in the toolbar.
An 'Export' button is present in the toolbar.

A validation status badge is present in the toolbar. On initial load with default YAML the badge should show 'Valid' (green) or 'Checking...' (muted) depending on whether validation has completed. It should never show 'Errors' for the default template.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and the 500ms validation debounce has elapsed

assertions.description: When the YAML editor contains a workflow with a 'name' field (e.g. 'name: "My Workflow"'), the workflow name input in the toolbar updates to match that name after validation completes. Conversely, if the user edits the name input directly, the displayed name changes but the YAML content in the editor is not automatically modified.
assertions.precondition: Valid YAML with a 'name' field has been entered and validation has completed

groups.name: Default YAML Template
groups.description: On first load the editor is pre-populated with a three-node example workflow. The graph pane should immediately render this as a valid 3-node linear chain.

assertions.description: The workflow name input shows 'My Workflow' on initial page load, matching the default YAML template's name field.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded for the first time with no imported workflow

assertions.description: After the default template validates, the toolbar and DAG Graph pane header both show '3 nodes' (the default template has step_1, step_2, step_3).
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and validation has completed (500ms elapsed)

assertions.description: After initial validation succeeds the status bar shows '3 nodes · workflow valid' on the left side.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and validation has completed

groups.name: Validation Status Badge States
groups.description: The toolbar validation badge cycles through five states: idle (Code2 icon, 'Not validated'), validating (pulsing icon, 'Checking...'), valid (green, 'Valid'), warning (yellow, 'Warnings'), and error (red, 'Errors'). The status bar also reflects these states with short messages.

assertions.description: While validation is in progress (within the 500ms debounce window after a change) the badge shows 'Checking...' text.
assertions.precondition: YAML content has just been modified and the 500ms debounce has not elapsed yet

assertions.description: When the YAML contains a validation error (e.g. a node with no type-discriminating field), the badge shows 'Errors' and an inline error snippet in red text appears to the right of the badge.
assertions.precondition: YAML contains invalid content and validation has completed

assertions.description: When there are validation errors, the status bar left side shows 'N error(s) detected' where N is the count of errors returned by the validator.
assertions.precondition: YAML contains validation errors and validation has completed

assertions.description: Validation follows this flow: (1) user types in the YAML editor, (2) badge transitions to 'Checking...' after 500ms debounce, (3) the Tauri command 'validate_dag_workflow' is invoked with the current YAML content, (4) on success the badge shows 'Valid' and node count updates, (5) on failure the badge shows 'Errors' and the first error message appears inline. If the backend command is unavailable, client-side js-yaml parsing is used as fallback with the same badge transitions.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and YAML editor contains valid workflow YAML

groups.name: Graph Pane Overlay States
groups.description: The ReactFlow graph pane shows one of three overlay states when the graph cannot be rendered: an empty-content message when the editor has no text, an error message when YAML is invalid, and a parsing spinner when YAML is valid but nodes haven't been laid out yet.

assertions.description: When the YAML editor is cleared to empty, the graph pane shows a centered overlay with the message 'Write a workflow in the editor to see the graph' and a GitBranch icon.

criteria.textContent: Write a workflow in the editor to see the graph

assertions.precondition: The YAML editor has been cleared (empty string)

assertions.description: When the YAML is syntactically or semantically invalid, the graph pane shows 'Fix YAML errors to see the graph' with an AlertTriangle icon. Up to 3 individual error messages are shown below the heading in red text.

criteria.textContent: Fix YAML errors to see the graph

assertions.precondition: The YAML editor contains content that fails validation

assertions.description: When the YAML is valid but no nodes have been parsed yet (transitional state between typing and graph render), the graph pane shows 'Parsing workflow...' with an animated spinner.
assertions.precondition: YAML is valid but graph computation has not completed yet

assertions.description: When valid YAML with at least one node is present, the graph overlay disappears and the ReactFlow canvas renders. Controls appear at bottom-left and a minimap at bottom-right of the graph pane.

target.label: DAG Graph pane with rendered graph

assertions.precondition: Valid YAML with at least one node has been entered and parsing is complete

groups.name: Node Type Rendering
groups.description: The DAG graph renders 8 distinct node types, each with a unique accent color and icon. Type is inferred from the presence of a type-discriminating YAML field: 'command' (blue, Terminal icon), 'prompt' (purple, MessageSquare), 'check_type' (amber, CheckCircle2), 'ui_bridge_action' (cyan, Layers), 'approval' (orange, ThumbsUp), 'cancel_reason' (red, XCircle), 'workflow_ref' (indigo, GitBranch), 'loop_body' (green, Repeat). Nodes with no recognized discriminator use a slate default.

assertions.description: Each graph node shows the node's 'name' field as its label. If no 'name' field is set, the node key (e.g. 'step_1') is used as the label. Labels are truncated to fit the node width.
assertions.precondition: Default YAML template is loaded and the graph has rendered

assertions.description: When a node's 'trigger_rule' is set to a value other than 'all_success' (the default), a small inline badge showing the trigger rule text appears inside the node card below the label. Nodes with trigger_rule 'all_success' or no trigger_rule show no badge.
assertions.precondition: A node with trigger_rule set to 'one_success', 'all_done', or 'none_failed_min_one_success' is in the YAML

assertions.description: The graph correctly identifies node types from YAML discriminator fields. A node with 'command:' field renders as a command node (blue). A node with 'prompt:' renders as a prompt node (purple). A node with 'approval:' renders as an approval node (orange). A node with 'workflow_ref:' renders as a workflow-ref node (indigo). The type detection is field-presence-based, not 'type:' key based.
assertions.precondition: YAML with mixed node types has been entered and the graph has rendered

assertions.description: Edges between nodes represent 'depends_on' relationships. Node B having 'depends_on: [nodeA]' must produce a directed edge from nodeA to nodeB (source=nodeA, target=nodeB). The edge uses a smoothstep curve with an arrowhead at the target end. Edges for unknown node IDs in depends_on are silently skipped (the unknown dep is not rendered).
assertions.precondition: YAML with at least two nodes where one depends_on the other has been entered and the graph has rendered

groups.name: Graph Layout and Navigation Controls
groups.description: The graph uses dagre top-to-bottom layout (rankdir=TB). ReactFlow controls appear at bottom-left of the graph pane (zoom in/out, fit view). A minimap appears at bottom-right. The graph supports scroll-to-zoom and drag-to-pan.

assertions.description: The ReactFlow controls panel is visible at the bottom-left of the graph pane when the graph has nodes. It contains zoom-in, zoom-out, and fit-view buttons.
assertions.precondition: Valid YAML with at least one node is rendered in the graph pane

assertions.description: A minimap is visible at the bottom-right of the graph pane when the graph has nodes. It provides an overview of the full DAG when the viewport is zoomed in.
assertions.precondition: Valid YAML with at least one node is rendered in the graph pane

assertions.description: Nodes are laid out top-to-bottom: root nodes (no depends_on) appear at the top; nodes with dependencies appear below their dependencies. A three-node linear chain (step_1 → step_2 → step_3) should display as a vertical column with step_1 at top and step_3 at bottom.
assertions.precondition: Default YAML template is loaded with a linear chain of 3 nodes

groups.name: Split-Pane Resize Handle
groups.description: A draggable vertical divider between the YAML editor and graph panes allows the user to adjust the width ratio. The minimum pane width is 20% and the maximum is 80% (of the total container width). The initial split is 50/50.

assertions.description: A draggable resize handle is rendered between the YAML editor pane and the DAG graph pane. It shows a GripVertical icon on hover and changes the cursor to col-resize.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded

assertions.description: Dragging the resize handle updates both pane widths proportionally. The left pane cannot shrink below 20% nor expand beyond 80% of the container. After resizing, both panes remain usable and the Monaco editor and ReactFlow canvas reflow correctly.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and both panes are visible

groups.name: Import and Export
groups.description: The Import button opens a Tauri file-picker dialog filtered to .yaml/.yml files; the selected file's content replaces the editor content and triggers re-validation. The Export button opens a Tauri save dialog with a default filename derived from the workflow name (spaces → underscores, .yaml extension); on save the last-saved timestamp appears in the status bar.

assertions.description: Clicking the Import button opens a native Tauri file picker dialog restricted to .yaml and .yml files. If the user selects a file, its content is loaded into the Monaco editor and re-validation begins. If the user cancels, the editor content is unchanged.

Clicking the Export button opens a native Tauri save dialog with the default filename set to '{workflowName}.yaml' (spaces replaced with underscores). After a successful save the status bar shows 'Saved HH:MM' (the current time in 2-digit hour:minute format).
assertions.precondition: A workflow is loaded in the editor

assertions.description: After a successful export, the status bar shows a 'Saved HH:MM' timestamp on the right side. Before any export the timestamp is absent.
assertions.precondition: The Export action has been completed at least once

groups.name: YAML Schema Correctness — Domain Logic
groups.description: The DAG workflow YAML schema has well-defined validation rules enforced by both the Rust backend (via 'validate_dag_workflow') and a client-side validator in dag-schema.ts. A workflow is valid if: it has a non-empty 'name' field, a non-null 'nodes' object with at least one node, and each node has exactly one type-discriminating field present (prompt, command, check_type, ui_bridge_action, a11y_action, loop_body, approval, workflow_ref, or cancel_reason). The spec below describes what correct validation output looks like on the page so a workflow can verify the validator is working correctly.

assertions.description: A node with no type-discriminating field (none of: prompt, command, check_type, ui_bridge_action, a11y_action, loop_body, approval, workflow_ref, cancel_reason) must cause the validation badge to show 'Errors' and the graph pane to show 'Fix YAML errors to see the graph'. The error snippet in the toolbar should reference the node path (e.g. 'nodes.my_node must have at least one of:').
assertions.precondition: YAML contains a node with no type-discriminating field

assertions.description: A node whose 'depends_on' list references a node ID that does not exist in the workflow must cause a validation error. The error should mention the unknown node ID and the referencing node's path (e.g. 'nodes.step_2.depends_on[0] references unknown node "missing_step"').
assertions.precondition: YAML contains a node with depends_on referencing a non-existent node ID

assertions.description: A YAML document missing the top-level 'name' field, or with an empty name ('name: ""'), must cause a validation error and the badge must show 'Errors'. A workflow with a valid name and valid nodes must show 'Valid'.
assertions.precondition: YAML is missing the name field or has empty name

assertions.description: The 'trigger_rule' field on a node accepts only four values: 'all_success', 'one_success', 'all_done', 'none_failed_min_one_success'. Any other value must produce a validation error. Valid trigger rules must not cause errors. The default (no trigger_rule field) is 'all_success' and is valid.
assertions.precondition: YAML contains a node with an invalid trigger_rule value (e.g. 'trigger_rule: always')

groups.name: Approval Dialog Overlay
groups.description: The ApprovalDialog component is mounted at the app level (not inside the DAG editor page) and listens globally for 'dag:approval-requested' Tauri events. When an approval node in a running workflow reaches the user-gate, this dialog appears as a fixed full-screen overlay requiring the user to Approve or Reject before execution can continue.

assertions.description: The approval dialog overlay is not visible when no approval request is pending. The dialog returns null and renders nothing to the DOM.
assertions.precondition: No DAG workflow with an approval node is currently running

assertions.description: When a 'dag:approval-requested' Tauri event fires, the overlay appears with the heading 'Approval Required' and a ShieldCheck (amber) icon.
assertions.precondition: A dag:approval-requested event has been received by the frontend

assertions.description: The approval dialog shows two buttons: 'Reject' (danger/red variant, ShieldX icon) and 'Approve' (success/green variant, ShieldCheck icon). Both are disabled while the response is being processed to prevent double-submission.
assertions.precondition: The approval dialog is visible

assertions.description: If the approval event payload includes 'node_name', the dialog shows 'Node: {node_name}' in small text below the 'Approval Required' heading.
assertions.precondition: The approval dialog is visible and the event payload included a node_name

assertions.description: Clicking 'Approve' invokes the Tauri command 'respond_dag_approval' with approved=true and the matching approval_id. Clicking 'Reject' invokes it with approved=false. After either action, the dialog disappears (request is cleared). The backend uses the approval_id to unblock the waiting DagApprovalHandler future, resuming or aborting workflow execution.
assertions.precondition: The approval dialog is visible with an active approval request

groups.name: Graph-to-YAML Correspondence — Domain Logic
groups.description: The graph is derived from the YAML by parsing the 'nodes' map and 'depends_on' lists. The graph must accurately reflect the YAML: one node per YAML node key, one edge per depends_on entry, and layout placing dependents below their dependencies. These assertions specify what correct graph-to-YAML mapping looks like so a workflow can verify the parser.

assertions.description: The number of nodes rendered in the ReactFlow graph must equal the number of keys in the YAML 'nodes' map. The node count shown in the toolbar badge and DAG Graph header badge must also match this count. If the YAML has 5 node keys, exactly 5 nodes must appear in the graph and the badges must show '5 nodes'.
assertions.precondition: Valid YAML with a known number of nodes has been entered and the graph has rendered

assertions.description: The graph must not render edges for depends_on entries that reference non-existent node IDs. If node_b has depends_on: [node_a, missing_node] and missing_node is not in the YAML nodes map, the graph silently renders only the node_a → node_b edge. No edge to a phantom node should appear.
assertions.precondition: YAML contains a depends_on entry referencing a non-existent node

assertions.description: Nodes with no shared dependency chain (parallel branches) should appear at the same vertical level in the graph. Two nodes that both depend on the same parent node but do not depend on each other should be side-by-side, not stacked vertically.
assertions.precondition: YAML contains parallel branches (two or more nodes depending on the same parent with no inter-dependency)

states.name: Editor Idle — Default Content
states.description: Page loaded with default YAML template. Validation has completed and the badge shows 'Valid'. The graph renders a 3-node linear chain.

transitions.name: Start editing YAML
transitions.description: User types in the Monaco YAML editor, triggering validation debounce

transitions.name: Click Import
transitions.description: User clicks the Import button to open file picker

states.name: Editor Validating
states.description: YAML content has changed and the validation debounce is active or the Tauri command is in-flight. Badge shows 'Checking...'.

transitions.name: Validation succeeds
transitions.description: Backend returns valid=true, badge transitions to 'Valid'

transitions.name: Validation fails
transitions.description: Backend returns errors or js-yaml throws, badge transitions to 'Errors'

states.name: Editor Valid
states.description: YAML has passed validation. Badge shows 'Valid'. Graph pane renders nodes and edges. Status bar shows '{N} nodes · workflow valid'.

transitions.name: Export workflow
transitions.description: User clicks Export to save the current YAML to disk

states.name: Editor Has Errors
states.description: YAML contains validation errors. Badge shows 'Errors'. First error message snippet is visible in toolbar. Graph pane shows 'Fix YAML errors to see the graph' overlay. Status bar shows 'N error(s) detected'.

elements.textContent: Fix YAML errors to see the graph

transitions.name: User fixes YAML
transitions.description: User edits the YAML to correct errors, triggering new validation

states.name: Workflow Exported
states.description: User has successfully exported the workflow. Status bar shows 'Saved HH:MM' timestamp on the right side.

states.name: Approval Dialog Visible
states.description: An approval node in a running DAG workflow has paused execution and the 'dag:approval-requested' event was received. The full-screen overlay is visible with 'Approval Required' heading and Approve/Reject buttons. The background page (including the YAML editor) remains visible but non-interactive behind the overlay.

transitions.name: User approves
transitions.description: User clicks Approve, respond_dag_approval is invoked with approved=true, dialog closes

transitions.name: User rejects
transitions.description: User clicks Reject, respond_dag_approval is invoked with approved=false, dialog closes

scenarios.name: Default template validates as valid

scenarios.name: Node missing type-discriminating field shows error
scenarios.description: Clear the editor and type YAML with a node that has no type field; assert Errors badge and graph overlay

waitForValidation.description: Wait for validation badge to leave 'Checking...' state

dag-validation-states.notes: Validation tests require the Rust backend to be running for the full Tauri command path. Client-side fallback can be tested without backend.

scenarios.name: Approval dialog appears when dag:approval-requested event fires
scenarios.description: Simulate a dag:approval-requested Tauri event and verify the overlay appears with correct content
scenarios.hardnessReason: Requires real Tauri event emission from backend, cannot be simulated with DOM fixtures alone

waitForApprovalDialog.description: Wait for approval dialog overlay to appear after event fires

dag-approval-dialog.notes: Full approval flow testing requires a live DAG workflow with an approval node to be running. The dialog hidden-by-default check is easy and fully automatable.
